one_line: Two young scholar-officials of the Maitraka-era Valabhi university, trained in Buddhist thought, practical governance, law and commerce.

appearance.face: Gunamati has an oval face, warm wheatish complexion, straight brows and calm, observant eyes with a gentle half-smile; Sthiramati has a slightly sharper jaw, similar wheatish tone, livelier eyes and a focused, determined expression.
appearance.hair: Both have straight, dark brown-black hair tied in modest topknots; Gunamati’s knot is smooth and centered, wrapped with a thin red cloth band, while Sthiramati’s is slightly tousled with a simple dark brown wooden hairpin; no additional headwear.
appearance.costume: Gunamati wears a knee-length off-white cotton angarkha-style upper robe with a wrap front tied at the right, over a pale saffron dhoti wrapped to the ankles in western Indian style, with a light, narrow-border shawl in muted maroon draped over the left shoulder; he has simple leather sandals, a thin copper bangle on the right wrist and a small palm-leaf manuscript pouch at his belt. Sthiramati wears a similar angarkha in soft pale grey-blue cotton with fine cross-hatching texture, over a deep indigo dhoti tied at the waist and reaching the ankles, and a light beige shawl folded neatly over both shoulders like a stole; he also wears sandals, a plain bronze finger ring on his right hand and a cloth belt with a few hanging wooden tally sticks and a small coin purse, signalling economic and administrative study; both are modestly and fully clothed in era-appropriate draped garments.
appearance.signature: A shared, slightly worn rectangular palm-leaf manuscript bundle wrapped in a maroon cloth with a simple cord, held in Gunamati’s hand while Sthiramati supports it; the visible palm leaves are bound with two wooden sticks, symbolizing their combined training in Buddhist learning, law, niti and varta.

ref_desc: Gunamati and Sthiramati are two lean, wheatish-complexioned young men with tied topknots, wearing angarkha robes over dhotis with maroon and indigo shawls, simple sandals and copper-bronze ornaments, jointly holding a maroon-wrapped palm-leaf manuscript bundle in a palette of off-white, saffron, maroon, indigo and pale grey-blue.
sheet_prompt: Draw two full-body shonen-anime style young male scholars, Gunamati and Sthiramati of Maitraka-era Valabhi, standing side by side: both lean, wheatish complexions, oval faces, straight brows, large expressive eyes. Each has dark brown-black hair tied in a modest topknot; Gunamati’s knot is smooth with a thin red cloth band, Sthiramati’s slightly tousled with a simple dark brown wooden hairpin. Gunamati wears a knee-length off-white cotton angarkha-style wrap robe over a pale saffron dhoti to the ankles, with a muted maroon shawl draped over his left shoulder, simple leather sandals, and a thin copper bangle on his right wrist; a small pouch hangs at his belt. Sthiramati wears a pale grey-blue angarkha with subtle cross-hatching over a deep indigo ankle-length dhoti, a neatly folded light beige shawl over both shoulders, leather sandals, and a plain bronze ring on his right hand, with a cloth belt carrying wooden tally sticks and a small coin purse. Ensure they are fully and modestly clothed in historically plausible draped garments. In the center of the composition they jointly hold a worn rectangular palm-leaf manuscript bundle wrapped in maroon cloth and bound with two wooden sticks, Gunamati supporting it more gently while Sthiramati grips it firmly. Use a harmonious palette of off-white, pale saffron, maroon, indigo, and pale grey-blue, showing front, three-quarter and slight side angles within the same image to clarify hair, faces, robes, dhotis, shawls, sandals and the shared manuscript prop.
